subject: Request: 3yr Price Lock + 5% Uplift Cap for Acme Biometrics
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 3yr Price Lock + 5% Uplift Cap for Acme Biometrics

Team —

Quick escalation on ACME (ACME-2026-036). Fast summary:
- Account: Acme Biometrics (healthcare device maker)
- ACV: $1.2M (year 1), committed consumption model across 3 years
- Ask from customer: 36-month price lock on unit pricing and an annual uplift cap of 5% for years 2 and 3; they want a renewal protection clause that limits our ability to re-price more than the cap if market costs shift.

We've negotiated heavy usage guarantees and a 20% committed-discount vs list. Acme is willing to sign a 3-year committed contract if we give these guardrails — the economics keep CAC payback within plan and secures a strategic design-win in a regulated vertical. Procurement has pushed for explicit language for price lock + uplift cap in the MSA.

Why I need exec signoff: this is a non-standard commercial term (multi-year price lock + explicit renewal protection). Legal flagged the renewal-protection language as risky without a narrowly defined carve-out for material cost increases (GPU price, cloud egress, third-party model licensing). Sales can absorb the discount, but we need approval to accept the uplift cap and the specific renewal protection language.

Proposal (what I'm asking you to approve):
1) Approve 36-month firm price lock at the negotiated unit rates as long as aggregate usage meets the committed minimums.
2) Approve a hard uplift cap of 5% YoY for years 2 and 3 on list-equivalent unit price, irrespective of model/infra cost movements, but with a limited carve-out: if our per-token service costs increase >25% due to third-party license or tariff changes, Sales & Legal can trigger a renegotiation (not an automatic pass-through).
3) Approve the inclusion of a renewal-protection paragraph that guarantees the cap for the 36-month term and obligates us to provide 90 days notice before any proposed changes at renewal.

Attachments: redwood-acme-36mo-term-sheet.pdf (term-sheet) and redwood-acme-redlines.docx (legal redlines from Acme).

Timing: They need a countersigned MSA + SOW to hit their procurement window — target close by 2026-03-10 (EOW next week). If we want to preserve the expansion ARR opportunity this quarter, ask for an exec yes/no by EOD 2026-03-05 or latest by 10am PT 2026-03-06 so I can coordinate legal and send DocuSign.

Risks: potential precedent for future deals; carve-out definition needs legal precision to avoid unlimited passthroughs.

My recommendation: approve (1) and (2) as written with (3) and the carve-out language to be finalized by Legal.

Thanks — will stand by.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 3yr Price Lock + 5% Uplift Cap for Acme Biometrics

Rishi —

Thanks for the concise summary. I agree this is strategically valuable but non-standard. Two quick asks before final:
1) Get Legal to draft a tight definition of "material cost increase" (exact triggers, metric, and calculation window).
2) I want Finance/FP&A to confirm runway impact modeling (we can't take a hit to margin that compromises this quarter's targets).

Marissa and Markus — can you two weigh in with the legal/finance risk tolerance? If both are OK with the carve-out language and Finance confirms the modeled impact <= 3% operating margin compression over the next 12 months, I'll greenlight. If not, escalate to Sophie/CTO for a final call.

Also loop in the customer procurement contact so we can get their redline priorities (Rishi, do that next).

— Lauren
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Acme Biometrics Procurement <procurement@acme-biometrics.com>, Hannah Li <hannah.li@acme-biometrics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA and term-sheet (ACME) — follow-up and executive review

Hannah / Acme procurement —

Thanks for the rapid turnaround on the redlines. Per our call, Redwood is prepared to move forward with a 36-month committed agreement. We are escalating internally for signoff on the price lock + uplift cap language; I wanted to share the internal ask and expected timeline so you have visibility.

To be explicit: Redwood's current proposed guardrails are 36 months of fixed unit pricing subject to meeting committed minimum usage, and an annual uplift cap of 5% in years 2 and 3. We will include a narrowly scoped carve-out for material cost increases that allows for a renegotiation conversation if our third-party costs increase >25% — that carve-out does not represent an automatic pass-through.

Attached: redwood-acme-36mo-term-sheet.pdf and our proposed redlines (redwood-acme-redlines.docx). We'll send the DocuSign once internal approvals are complete. Do you have any hard veto points on the renewal-protection clause?

DocuSign preview: https://docusign.com/ABC-ACME-36MO

Looking to finalize by EOD 2026-03-10.

Regards,
Rishi
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 3yr Price Lock + 5% Uplift Cap for Acme Biometrics

Rishi / Lauren —

I reviewed the redlines and the proposed carve-out. Finance is OK to approve the 5% uplift cap and the 36-month price lock contingent on two items:
1) Legal signs off on the carve-out language such that any cost-triggered change requires prior CFO-level approval and an explicit 60-day notice period.
2) We include an audit clause allowing us to verify committed minimums quarterly (standard monitoring, no penalty if usage shortfalls are remedied in a subsequent quarter).

If Legal agrees to those guardrails, mark me as approved to proceed. Please note the precedence risk — we should catalog this as a special approved deviation with a replicability review for similar strategic accounts.

Onward.
— Markus
